text:
**Short version:** Qi2 is the open standard, Qi2.2 is its faster 25W update, and MagSafe is Apple's own branding and implementation of the same magnetic idea.

| | Qi2 | Qi2.2 (Qi2 25W) | MagSafe |
|---|---|---|---|
| Who | Wireless Power Consortium (WPC) | WPC | Apple |
| Top speed | 15W | 25W | 15W on most iPhones, up to 25W on newer ones |
| Magnets | Yes, magnetic ring for alignment | Yes | Yes |

**Qi2** added a magnetic ring to Qi wireless charging, with Apple contributing MagSafe technology to the standard. The magnets keep the phone aligned, which improves efficiency and speed ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/708060/qi-2-2-certification-25w-wpc-belkin-anker-ugreen-aukey), [WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)).

**Qi2.2** is the formal name for Qi2 25W (spec v2.2.1, launched July 2025). It offers nearly 70% more power than Qi2, and WPC says it can charge a phone from 0 to 50% in about 30 minutes ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)).

**MagSafe** is Apple's version. Apple certifies MagSafe accessories for 15W on most iPhones and up to 25W on the iPhone 16 and 17 series. Certified MagSafe chargers also have an NFC antenna so the iPhone can identify them, and a magnetometer to prevent compass interference. In Macworld's tests, 15W MagSafe and 15W Qi2 chargers charged at about the same speed ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html)).

**Things to watch for**
- **"MagSafe-compatible" isn't MagSafe.** These are usually non-certified 7.5W chargers with a ring of magnets, and they charge about half as fast ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html)).
- **Your iPhone sets the real speed.** Per Apple, iPhone 17 and 18 Pro models and the 16 Plus and 16 Pro Max reach 25W, iPhone 16 and 16 Pro reach 22.5W, and iPhone Air reaches 20W. The iPhone 17e and iPhone 15 and earlier top out at 15W. You also need a 30W or greater adapter for 25W ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-ie/105047)). The iPhone 16e has no magnetic wireless charging.
- **Android support is thin.** The Pixel 10, 10 Pro and 10 Pro Fold do Qi2 at 15W, and the Pixel 10 Pro XL does Qi2.2 at 25W. Samsung's Galaxy S26 line is "Qi2 Ready," meaning it needs a magnetic case for 15W ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/939362/best-magsafe-qi2-2-batteries-power-banks)).
- **Look for the Qi2 logo.** Only WPC-certified products can show it, and you can check any product in WPC's database ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)).

**In practice:** Apple's own [MagSafe Charger](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m) is certified for both MagSafe and Qi2 25W, so one product covers all three. That link is the 2 m version at $49, and Macworld lists the 1 m version at $39. For an iPhone that tops out at 15W, any certified Qi2 charger will do the same job for less.

I can suggest specific chargers or power banks for your phone if you tell me which model you have.
